### Problem: Minimum cost to move chips {#sec-pf-p6-chips}

::: {.p-statement}
Chips sit at integer positions $p_1, \dots, p_n$ ($1 \le n \le 100$, $1 \le p_i \le 10^9$). Moving a chip by 2 is free; moving it by 1 costs 1. Find the minimum cost to gather all chips at one position.

Source: [LC 1217 · Minimum Cost to Move Chips to The Same Position](https://leetcode.com/problems/minimum-cost-to-move-chips-to-the-same-position/){.solved difficulty="Easy"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
Free moves preserve a chip's **parity**, and paid moves flip it. So a chip's position modulo 2 is the only thing that matters, and each chip whose parity differs from the target's costs exactly 1.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
**Invariant:** a chip's parity changes only on a paid move, and every paid move changes it. Gathering at a target $t$ costs at least the number of chips with parity $\ne t \bmod 2$, and exactly that is achievable (one paid move for each of them, everything else free). So the answer is $\min(\#\text{odd}, \#\text{even})$.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
#### Python

```{python}
#| label: pf-chips
def min_cost_chips(p):
    odd = sum(x % 2 for x in p)
    return min(odd, len(p) - odd)

def min_cost_chips_brute(p):
    """Shortest-path cost for each chip to each target (moves of +-1 cost 1, +-2 cost 0)."""
    return min(sum(abs(x - t) % 2 for x in p) for t in range(min(p), max(p) + 1))

for _ in range(1000):
    p = [random.randint(1, 20) for _ in range(random.randint(1, 10))]
    assert min_cost_chips(p) == min_cost_chips_brute(p)

assert min_cost_chips([1, 2, 3]) == 1
assert min_cost_chips([2, 2, 2, 3, 3]) == 2
assert min_cost_chips([1, 1000000000]) == 1
```

#### C++

```cpp
int minCostToMoveChips(const vector<int>& p) {
    int odd = 0;
    for (int x : p) odd += x & 1;
    return min(odd, (int)p.size() - odd);
}
```
:::

::: {#fig-pf-chips}

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
pos = [2, 2, 2, 3, 3]
assert min_cost_chips(pos) == 2
def draw(ax, p):
    counts = [pos.count(x) for x in range(1, 6)]
    V.grid(ax, p, [list(range(1, 6)), [c or "" for c in counts]], row_labels=["position", "chips"],
           colors={(1, i): ("indigo" if (i + 1) % 2 == 0 else "amber") for i, c in enumerate(counts) if c})
    V.text(ax, p, 5.6, -0.5, "even: 3 chips\nodd: 2 chips → cost 2", ha="left", color="violet")
V.show(draw)
```

Chips at [2, 2, 2, 3, 3]. Free ±2 moves keep parity, so all even chips can meet at 2 for free and all odd chips at 3 for free. Gathering costs one paid move per chip of the minority parity: 2.

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Time** $O(n)$. **Space** $O(1)$.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- All chips with the same parity: cost 0.
- Positions up to $10^9$: never iterate over positions; only parity matters.
:::
